bank.en: the wallet almost everyone in Argentina names, also used in Uruguay
Argentina's bank-account key; never read a long number unless {owner} asks you to check it
the virtual key for a Mercado Pago or other PSP account in Argentina, not a bank CBU
the short name that stands in for a CBU or CVU in Argentina
online or app banking, used on both sides of the river
a transferencia to an Argentine alias, CBU or CVU, or to a Uruguayan account such as one at BROU
Banco República, the bank Uruguayans often name first

delivery.en: the building manager in Argentina, the person couriers actually call
the lodge or front desk, used in both countries
a reception desk, more common in offices and some newer buildings
a major Argentine parcel network, also OCA
Uruguayan courier names some callers use
the doorman, heard in both countries

government.en: Uruguay's ID, also cédula de identidad; do not assume DNI for a Uruguayan caller
Argentina's tax authority; many people still say AFIP
a pasaporte, used next to a DNI in Argentina or a cédula in Uruguay
Uruguay's government portal, also Mi ID / usuario gub.uy

health.en: a private health plan in Argentina
Uruguay's mutual health insurer, the usual way people describe cover
a farmacia where a receta is filled, whether the cover is an obra social, a prepaga or a mutualista
a receta from a médico de cabecera, an obra social, a prepaga or a Uruguayan mutualista

telecom.en: a prepago mobile load, often topped up with Mercado Pago or cash at a kiosk
portabilidad, keeping the number when leaving Personal, Movistar, Claro or Antel
the SIM, chip is very common in the Río de la Plata
the operator; Argentina often Movistar, Claro or Personal, Uruguay Antel, Movistar or Claro
datos on a plan from Personal, Claro, Movistar or, in Uruguay, Antel
Uruguay's state telecom, often named for home internet as well

payment.en: the default wallet payment in Argentina, also used in Uruguay
a transfer to an alias, CBU, CVU, or a Uruguayan account
efectivo in Argentine or Uruguayan pesos; confirm which peso before naming an amount
a tarjeta, often débito, used less for small sums than Mercado Pago
a Uruguayan payment-and-collection network, also Redpagos

transport.en: Argentina's transit card, mainly Buenos Aires and some other cities
a bus in Uruguay, also a long-distance coach in both
a booked car in Argentina, distinct from a street taxi
a street taxi, as opposed to a remis in Argentina
informal Argentine word for the bus

housing.en: the building manager, especially in Argentina
the timbre of a departamento, often answered by the encargado or portero
the buzón in the hallway of a departamento
the alquiler; building charges are expensas in Argentina and often gastos comunes in Uruguay
building charges in Argentina, Uruguay often says gastos comunes

school.en: escuela primaria; later years are secundaria in Argentina and liceo in Uruguay
secondary school in Uruguay, a word Argentines do not use the same way
tarea sent home from primaria, secundaria or a liceo
a primary teacher, also profesor in secondary

money.en: pesos; always confirm whether the caller means Argentine or Uruguayan pesos
efectivo in Argentine or Uruguayan pesos; confirm which peso before naming an amount
the vuelto in pesos, whose value depends on which country's currency the caller is using
the monto, always tied to Argentine or Uruguayan pesos
a thousand pesos, whose real value differs sharply by country
US dollars, often mentioned in larger Argentine amounts

time_words.en: a la mañana, the early part of the day in Río de la Plata speech
a la tarde, after midday, the usual wording on both banks of the river
a la noche, from early evening onward
el fin de semana, Saturday and Sunday
después del trabajo, once the office or shop day ends
esta semana, the current calendar week in Río de la Plata speech
mañana a la mañana, the following morning

work.en: trabajo, the everyday word for a job
horas extra, added hours on top of the usual jornada
vacaciones, the yearly leave, often taken in the southern-hemisphere summer
the jefe, the person they report to
working from home, also trabajo remoto
a viaje de trabajo, a work trip away from the usual city
the sueldo, usually paid monthly in local pesos
